articles.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model designed to identify and validate exploitable vulnerabilities while staying within researcher-defined boundaries.

articles.title: INTRODUCING INKLING 2 SMALL
articles.summary: Inkling 2 Small is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 594B total parameters, 17B active, that supports image inputs and variable effort. The model's vision and agentic capabilities enable it to incorporate visual feedback to iteratively build and refine websites, games, and 3D designs with interactive elements. It will be initially available through Tinker with closed weights. Full weights will be available under an Apache 2.0 license next week after the completion of external safety testing and red-teaming.

articles.summary: Anthropic's AI R&D capabilities accelerated significantly, improving model performance on well-defined tasks at roughly twice the rate compared to 2024-2025. This acceleration primarily results from AI's increasing role in R&D, though multiple factors contributed in late 2025.

articles.title: CLOUDFLARE'S TRUST FRAMEWORK FOR AI AGENTS

articles.title: THE BENCHMARK WHERE AIS HAVE TO LIE TO WIN
articles.summary: Blood on the Clocktower is a social deception game. Watching AI play the game unveils a lot about how AI is progressing on a set of AI capabilities that no other benchmark gives clear visibility into. The game requires AI to execute schemes with creativity, on-the-spot bluffing, and collective reasoning. This post looks at what happens when you pit AI models against each other in the game.

articles.title: NVIDIA INTRODUCED VFLASH

articles.title: NEW NVIDIA COSMOS 3 OPEN MODELS FOR INTERACTIVE WORLD SIMULATION
articles.summary: NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 platform now offers four open-weight models for interactive world simulation and driving scenes, each with 16 billion trainable parameters. These models enable multi-sensor data generation, synchronized observations, and photorealistic video from simulator controls, supporting advanced research in robotics and autonomous driving.

articles.title: HOW PRIMARY COMPUTE MARKETS WORK
articles.summary: GPU providers sell capacity through reservations, on-demand rentals, and interruptible spot contracts. Reservations help secure financing through predictable revenue, on-demand offers flexibility at higher rates, and spot monetizes idle capacity. Ornn's compute price indices track executed on-demand transactions, excluding reservations and spot rentals.
